Team lead's note, Friday
Since Riddhi's promotion to senior analyst was announced on Monday, Binita has praised her in every meeting. "Riddhi is honestly a genius." "Nobody deserved it more." "We're so lucky to have her above us." Binita, who was also shortlisted for the role, said this at least five times in two days, once in the middle of a budget discussion. Her voice rises each time, and she laughs a little too quickly afterwards.
I don't read this as ill will. Binita has been generous and helpful all week. It may simply be a lot of feelings at once: disappointment, pride in a friend, awkwardness. I'm not going to guess out loud.
Next step: I've booked a one-to-one with Binita for Tuesday to talk about her growth plan and what the next opening could look like.
Tenzin

qa.a: She might feel flattered but also a little uneasy, sensing the praise is more than the moment needs.

14 August
Team-lead post announced today, and it's me. Ayesha, who applied for the same role, hugged me first. Then she told the whole floor, "She's the best choice, the best, honestly, I'd have picked her myself!" At lunch she said it again. In the lift she said it again, to the security guard. By evening she'd posted in the team chat: "SO deserved!!! 🎉"
Part of me felt celebrated. Part of me felt watched. It was too much, too often, and her jaw looked tight when she smiled.
But I also know Ayesha. She covered my shifts when Amma was in hospital. So I'm not going to decide she secretly hates me. Maybe she's happy and sad at the same time. I would be.
Tomorrow: ask her for coffee. Just the two of us. No promotion talk unless she brings it up.
Kavitha

qa.a: In the lift, to the security guard, and then in the team chat.

qa.q: What choice did Kavitha make about how to read Ayesha, and why is it wise?
qa.a: She decided not to assume hidden hate, remembering Ayesha's past kindness, and planned a quiet coffee, which leaves room for honest feelings. 🙂

qa.a: She may be truly happy for Kavitha and disappointed for herself at once, and the extra praise could be her way of handling both.

Ganga,

Something odd since my promotion. Farzana, who applied for the same role, has congratulated me every single day this week. Monday: a card. Tuesday: a speech at the team huddle about how I'm "the most deserving person in this entire building." Wednesday: a cake. Thursday: she told my manager, in front of me, that I'm a genius. Ishita

When I got the team-lead role in April, Jahnavi was the first to congratulate me. Then the second, and the fifth. She posted about it on the team channel, brought a cake with "Our Star Parveen" in blue icing, and told every visiting client, "Parveen is simply the best, honestly the best."
